title: Perplexity Teammates for Business - Always-On Agents With a Human Gate
content:
Chatbots answer one prompt. Businesses
need ongoing work with a HUMAN GATE.
Perplexity shipped Teammates — agents that
own complex, ongoing assignments, plan and
coordinate, and let you inspect and guide
them inside Computer.
Announced around early November 2026.
Initially on the web for individual Max
subscribers.
Stay for the permissions pattern and the
checklist I want every small business to
run before they hand an agent a refund
path.

Verified shape from Perplexity's Teammates
positioning and reporting.
Teammates own ongoing work. They plan,
coordinate, and work inside Computer with
tools and files.
You can inspect progress, redirect, or
take over the agent desktop when needed.
Changelog-style examples include a morning
inbox draft, a competitor watch, and a
support email path with a line like CHECK
WITH ME BEFORE ANY REFUND.
Help-center style guidance: research
preview for individual Max; isolated
computers; plugins with the same
permissions you grant; credentials
encrypted so teammates cannot view them.
TechRepublic reports Max at about 200
DOLLARS PER MONTH, or 2,000 dollars
annually. Free and Pro users can upgrade
to Max if they want this class of agent.
I am not citing unverified social stats
like 7x agent-hours or 10,000 teammates.
Stick to primary product claims.

Business how-to.
Step 1: name one recurring workflow. Inbox
triage. Competitor watch. Support draft.
Not five workflows on day one.
Step 2: connect only the plugins that job
needs. LEAST PRIVILEGE. If the agent does
not need send-mail, do not grant
send-mail.
Step 3: require human approval for
refunds, outbound sends, charges, and
publishes.
Step 4: keep a weekly inspect and redirect
ritual. Open the thread. Read what
changed. Redirect or take over the
desktop.
Say you run a 12-person support desk. The
teammate drafts replies overnight. A human
still taps send. That is a labelled
example, not a case study I ran.

I put the pattern into a free checklist
for small business.
Sections: pick one recurring workflow.
Permissions with least-privilege plugins
only. Human gates for refund, send,
charge, publish. Isolated computer plus
credential rules. Weekly inspect and
redirect ritual. A 7-DAY PILOT LOG that
captures approve, edit, and reject
reasons.
Sources on the checklist: Perplexity
Teammates blog, changelog examples, and
help-center permission notes.
Comment AI on Instagram and I'll send you
the free PDF. Or grab the link in the
LinkedIn post.
DM me if you want this for your business.

What not to automate on day one.
Do not let an always-on agent issue
refunds unsupervised.
Do not connect every SaaS plugin because
the demo looked cool.
Do not skip the isolated computer model —
shared credentials across agents is how
incidents start.
Do not confuse Max pricing with enterprise
rollout. TechRepublic notes individual Max
first; broader enterprise availability is
still an open planning question.
Pilot one workflow for 7 days. Log every
human edit. Then decide whether to expand.

Here's my take.
Always-on agents are useful when the job
is ongoing and the irreversible actions
stay behind a human gate.
Perplexity Teammates productize inspect,
redirect, and take-over. Your job is to
write the gates before you celebrate
autonomy.
Assistants without gates are liability.
Teammates with gates are leverage.
